newsitem.title: UK: Novorossiisk crude loading delays grow - trade.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk crude loading delays grow - trade.

text.p: The delay in loading crude oil tankers from Russia's main export port, Novorossiisk in the Black Sea, grew by another 3-4 days to 9-10 days on Thursday as bad weather exacerbated the effect of maintenance on the pipeline feeding the port, Mediterranean crude traders said.
"First Transneft delayed loadings by 5-6 days due to pipeline maintenance, now we expect another 3-4 days delay because of the weather," an Italian refiner said.
"There is a big confusion in Novorossiisk. No-one knows when their cargoes are going to load," he added.
During the first 11 days in September, Novorossiisk has suspended loadings for roughly six days due to thunderstorms, large swell or high winds, according to a shipping inspector.
Berthing was suspended on Thursday morning due to high winds and swell, although vessels already alongside were able to load, the inspector said.
A trader at an Italian refiner said Novorossiisk's main pipeline, which feeds the port with 85 percent of its crude, is due to close for maintenance for four days from September 20.

Urals prices have already jumped 20 cents to Dated Brent -80 cents in the past week and refiners say the crude is still in strong demand because of the historically low high/low sulphur fuel oil spread.
"A high/low spread of $8.00 (per tonne) is amazing, so Urals is one of the best grades," the Italian refiner said.
